short: Allied leaders met in Morocco to plan the European strategy and announce the doctrine of unconditional surrender.
full:
Between 14 and 24 January 1943, US President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met at the Casablanca Conference in French Morocco. Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin declined to attend due to the ongoing Battle of Stalingrad. The leaders agreed to prioritize the strategic bombing of Germany, the invasion of Sicily and mainland Italy, and the continued buildup of forces in Britain for an eventual cross-Channel invasion.

At the conclusion of the conference, Roosevelt announced that the Allies would accept nothing less than the unconditional surrender of the Axis powers. This demand was intended to reassure the Soviet Union of Western commitment and prevent any separate peace treaties. It shaped the final stages of the war by precluding negotiated settlements with the Axis regimes.
